text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Redwood SLO breach detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2. p95 latency 2.4s (SLO=1.2s), p99 7.1s. Streaming stalls spikes observed from 15:03-15:16 UTC. Auto-mitigation attempted: fallback to model-quant-128 triggered for 120s. Paging eng-oncall.

alice: got the page, I'm on it. grabbing recent dashboards now. @dmitri you'll want to take logs for the prefill workers if you're free?

dmitri: oncall ack. pulling kv-cache metrics and prefill queues. preliminary: cache pressure on kv-prefill partition, eviction rate spiked ~15:05. Looks like fragmentation + prefill vs decode imbalance — prefill tasks are allocating large KV chunks and decode is struggling to reclaim.

eva: seeing same on the dashboard. streaming stalls correlate with decode tasks waiting on KV reads. p95 jump matches reads latency increase. link: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/us-west-2/kv?from=15:00&to=15:20

ben: any customer reports yet? maggie-cs?

maggie-cs: 2 customers reported intermittent stalls in chat sessions (~15:06). One reported partial transcripts repeating after delay. Escalated to enterprise@; I'm updating them that we're triaging and will provide ETA.

alice: quick triage plan: 1) confirm scope (regions, models, customers) 2) try emergency mitigations: a) increase prefill eviction threshold, b) shard / reroute heavy tenants to fallback pool, c) temporarily reduce prefetch depth, d) enable force-evict on low-usage KV buckets. 3) gather logs for postmortem.

dmitri: confirming scope: us-west-2 only so far, model-family oak-2 and oak-2-quant. Affected routes show heavy prefix reuse sets which blow up KV segment counts. I can run quick lsof/ps on prefill workers and sample KV segments.

ops-bot: Running runbook: "kv-cache-pressure" -> step 1: surface eviction rate, step 2: adjust eviction target, step 3: if p99>5s escalate to SE.

alice: do we want to try increasing allocation to prefill cache? we have limited headroom but can borrow from image-cache for 5 minutes.

dmitri: yes, propose: echo 0.15 > /sys/cache/prefill/watermark ; increase by 15%. Command: 
```
# increase prefill watermark (temporary)
kubectl -n runtime exec -it prefill-config -- sh -c "echo 0.15 > /proc/sys/redwood/prefill_watermark"
```
This should reduce eviction churn and give decode time to catch up.

eva: I'm concerned about fragmentation — simply raising watermark might delay eviction but not fix fragmented slabs. We should also trigger a targeted compaction on aged KV segments.

ben: how risky is compaction live? will it add CPU pressure and worsen stalls?

dmitri: compaction is CPU heavy but can be rate-limited. Plan: 1) bump prefill_watermark, 2) enable compaction at low rate for partitions with >70% fragmentation: 
```
# limited compaction
kubectl -n runtime exec -it kv-operator -- sh -c "kvctl compact --partitions us-west-2-prefill --rate=5MB/s"
```
Monitor CPU. If CPU>70% for decode workers, stop compaction.

alice: proceed with bump + low-rate compaction. dmitri, execute and post immediate metrics.

dmitri: executing now.

incident-bot: ACTION: increased prefill_watermark to 0.15 at 15:08:12 UTC by dmitri. Compact command issued rate=5MB/s.

dmitri: initial effect: eviction rate dropped 40% within 40s. p95 trending down from 2.4s -> 1.6s at 15:10. p99 still high at ~5.6s but improving. streaming stalls reduced, but a small cohort still seeing stalls.

eva: checked decode worker CPU: went from 42% -> 61% during compaction window. under threshold. Good.

maggie-cs: told customers we see improvements and to expect restored behavior in ~10-20m. they asked for root cause — I'll hold until we have more clarity.

alice: good progress. next: identify heavy tenants to move off hot partition. dmitri can you list top 10 tenant IDs by prefill allocations?

dmitri: listing... 
```
# kvctl top-tenants
tenant-42: 28% prefill allocation
tenant-88: 12%
tenant-7: 9%
...rest <6%
```
Tenant-42 is huge; they are running many long-chat sessions. Recommend transiently throttling their prefill concurrency or redirecting to fallback-dedicated pool.

eva: fallback pool ready? we have a spare small pool with quantized model in us-west-2-dedicated-1.

alice: let's move tenant-42 traffic to fallback pool for 30m. ben, coordinate with traffic-router and update rate-limits.

ben: initiating reroute for tenant-42 -> us-west-2-dedicated-1. Command:
```
trafficctl route set --tenant tenant-42 --target us-west-2-dedicated-1 --timeout 00:30:00
```

ops-bot: Reroute job queued. Expected propagation ~30s.

incident-bot: REROUTE: tenant-42 now routing to us-west-2-dedicated-1 (propagated at 15:12:01 UTC).

dmitri: after reroute, prefill allocation for hotspot partition dropped from 78% -> 56% within 90s. p95 -> 1.2s, p99 -> 3.1s at 15:14. Streaming stalls mostly gone, only sporadic at tail.

maggie-cs: customers confirming improved latency, one says they still see occasional stalls but much better. sending update to enterprise.

alice: good. status: mitigated but not resolved. temporary fixes: watermark bump, targeted compaction, tenant reroute. Next actions: 1) keep compaction running until fragmentation <35%, 2) add targeted eviction rule for small KV buckets, 3) schedule postmortem and long term fix (better slab allocator + prefill quotas), 4) notify product/security if any sensitive requests were affected.

dmitri: I'll keep an eye and collect logs for postmortem. saving kv-snapshot for the impacted partition.

dmitri: saved snapshot: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2937654321/kv-snapshot-uw2-prefill-2026-03-15T15-16Z.tar.gz

eva: adding temporary metric alarms to warn earlier: lower threshold for eviction-rate and fragmentation ratio.

ben: coordinating with router and infra to make reroute sticky. I'll also open a support ticket to discuss rate-limits with tenant-42's account team.

maggie-cs: I've notified customers and set expectation for postmortem by EOD. they requested to be CC'd.

alice: handoff to dmitri for full follow-up. I'll go offline for a few mins but remain on pager. Summary for handoff: 
- Incident: KV prefill fragmentation/pressure causing decode stalls, us-west-2, oak-2 models, start 15:03 UTC
- Mitigations executed: bump prefill_watermark -> 0.15; targeted compaction rate-limited; rerouted tenant-42 to fallback pool; reduced prefetch depth on 2 nodes.
- Result: p95 restored to SLO (~1.2s), p99 improved to ~3.1s (still above 1.2 but acceptable for mitigation); customer impact reduced, live sessions stabilized.
- Postmortem artifacts: kv-snapshot link, metrics dashboard, logs marker IDs: 2937654321-logs-1..6

dmitri: taking over. I'll keep the compaction running until fragmentation <30% and then step down. I'll also schedule a postmortem doc and assign owners. tagging @eng-ml for allocator review.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> partial-resolved at 15:16:12 UTC. Monitoring for regression for 2h.

alice: thank you everyone. please file follow-ups:
- dmitri: postmortem + slab allocator proposal (owner)
- eva: alarms & runbook update for fragmentation (owner)
- ben: tenant throttling policy + routing automation (owner)
- maggie-cs: customer comms & CC list (owner)

maggie-cs: noted, will email enterprise and add them to the postmortem watcher list.

dmitri: quick notes for postmortem: probable root cause = sustained high-prefix reuse causing many tiny KV writes that fragment slabs; prefill was too aggressive on allocation and decode reclaimed slower due to a micro-regression in async-io. Long term: implement slab defragmentation, per-tenant prefill quotas, and add async-io backpressure.

eva: adding one more: add a canary task to simulate high-prefix reuse workload to catch regressions.

alice: closing loop: if p99 climbs again re-open page and escalate to SE. otherwise we'll follow up in PM. thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Auto-note: incident created id=INC-2937654321, severity=sev2, assigned=eng-oncall, postmortem-due=2026-03-16.

maggie-cs: customer update sent at 15:25. they acknowledged and asked for a follow-up with remediation timeline.

dmitri: will draft postmortem and assign reviewers. setting follow-up meeting 16:30 UTC to review initial findings.

alice: thanks — handoff complete."
